briefs.polymarket-6443529: The question asks whether Elon Musk's @elonmusk account will log between 180 and 199 posts from 12:00 PM ET on Nov 3 to 12:00 PM ET on Nov 10, 2026, as shown by the xtracker.io Post Counter. The counter includes main-feed posts, quote posts and reposts, and counts replies that appear on the main feed; deleted posts count if the tracker captured them within about five minutes, and community reposts the tracker misses do not count. The research could not open xtracker.io, so no counted weekly series for 2026 exists, and there is no count yet for Nov 3 to Nov 5. The only hard figure is a 2025 analysis attributed to NBC News, which put Musk at about 1,716 posts between Sept 17 and Oct 17, 2025, over 55 a day or roughly 390 a week (https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/science/elon-musk-s-x-activity-49-posts-on-politics-often-fringe/story, not checked against the original). A 180-199 week works out to about 26 to 28 posts a day, so it would need a pace around half of that 2025 average. Search results show weekly count brackets for Oct to Nov 2026 weeks ranging from 80-99 and 100-119 up to 260-279, 300-319 and 500+, and a listing of the xtracker rules sits at https://explorer.struct.to/markets/elon-musk-of-tweets-november-7-november-14-140-159 (not checked); these show the spread of possible outcomes, not which ones happened. The base rate was therefore built by treating the 2025 pace as the central scenario and the bracket range as the width: counts vary widely week to week, so a single 20-post bucket in the lower part of the range holds only a modest share of the probability. What is different this time: the window opens the day of the Nov 3, 2026 US midterm elections and runs through the aftermath, a period when political news would normally push Musk's posting up rather than down. The case for other outcomes is that a 2025-like pace, or a heavier election-week pace, would put the total well above 199, and brackets of 260 and higher appear in the listings. For this bucket to hit, his activity would have to fall far below the 2025 pace, for example because of a travel or work-heavy week or an account change. Unknowns that could change the answer: the actual tracker counts for Nov 3 to Nov 5, the recent 2026 weekly totals, whether his 2026 posting rate is lower than in 2025, and how the tracker handles deleted posts and community reposts. A first-days count near 25 a day or lower would raise the chance materially, while a count of 40 or more a day would make this bucket close to impossible.
